Stratospheric Plume Sampling Lab

A virtual sampling instrument for the coupled plume simulations: one tonne of SO₂ released into the stratosphere. Step through time in 30-minute increments, read off the in-plume values an aircraft would measure, switch on measurement noise, and export the record for your own inverse-modeling analysis.
Loading model runs…
?The aged and young stratospheric air states (distinguished by their N₂O) are anchored in measurements from the NOAA SABRE field campaign; see the Science paper. The SAI-deployed state represents a stratosphere already seeded with injected aerosol. ?Both releases sit in the lower stratosphere: it starts near 20 km at 30°N but closer to 15 km at 60°N, where the tropopause is lower.
?Multiplicative lognormal noise, obs = truth·exp(σz): every observed quantity gets an independent draw per 30-minute time bin, reproducible from the seed. The dilution factor is the known mixing model and stays exact; every dilution-corrected value is recomputed from the noisy observations.

Every value on this page is output from a coupled chemistry, microphysics, and photolysis model of one plume; the day/night shading follows the model's own photolysis rates. The dilution factor V(t)/V₀ is the analytic mixing schedule the model itself used, so the passive tracer (which the model does not carry) is exact: C/C₀ = V₀/V. Each case runs until the plume's surface area has stayed within 10% of the background for a full day.

The model architecture, validation, and documentation live on GitHub.
